title: Usage stream guardian: heuristic validator and TTL archiver
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a lightweight, edge-stage service — 'stream-guardian' — for the Console usage pipeline that performs fast heuristic validation, soft-schema repair, deduplication, and TTL-based archiving of late events before they reach the main schema-enforced store. Goal: reduce downstream schema rejections and noisy alerts while preserving high throughput and low ingress latency. The service will provide both hard-reject and soft-repair modes, a fallback queue for suspect events, and a TTL archiver to keep transient late-arriving telemetry for N days for forensic analysis.
acceptance_criteria: 99.5% of syntactically invalid events are caught and routed to the fallback queue or auto-repaired with an audit trail
End-to-end extra latency at ingress no greater than +15ms p95 when at steady-state RPS
TTL archiver stores late/repairable events for configurable retention and exposes a queryable index for SRE/analysis
Dashboard metrics and alerts for repair_rate, fallback_queue_size, avg_validation_latency, and dropped_events
Integration tests covering behavior across 3 failure modes: malformed payloads, schema drift (missing fields), and duplicate event bursts
implementation_notes: Prototype implemented as a small Go service using fastjson for parsing to minimize allocations
Validation pipeline: quick syntactic checks -> heuristic field typing -> canonicalizer -> soft-repair -> dedupe -> either accept or route to fallback queue
Soft-repair rules are editable via a ruleset stored in Config Store; defaults include timestamp coercion, enum normalization, and pointer-to-root promotion for nested user_id variants
Deduplication uses a sliding window bloom filter + LRU cache with tunable TTL to avoid O(N) state on high-cardinality keys
Fallback queue implemented on top of existing Kafka topic 'usage.fallback' with a dead-letter TTL and a small repair worker pool
Provide toggles for 'silent mode' (metrics only) and 'strict mode' (hard reject) for rollout/experimentation
performance_benchmarks: Local benchmark: 10k RPS sustained with p95 validation latency 9ms (single replica on c5.4xlarge-equivalent)
Staging run: when parallelized across 6 replicas achieved 60k RPS with ingestion CPU at 68% and added median latency ~7ms
Initial sampling on production shadowing reduced downstream schema-rejection noise by ~72% across sampled routes (from 6.2% invalid to 1.7%)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: heuristics may over-correct and change semantics -> Mitigation: all repairs go to audit trail and must be reversible, and repairs require explicit opt-in per route
Risk: added latencies could violate SLOs for low-latency routes -> Mitigation: per-route bypass flags and an emergency fast-path that applies only syntactic checks
Risk: fallback queue growth during incidents -> Mitigation: backpressure signals to upstream producers and autoscaling repair worker pool with circuit-breaker throttles
